title.zh: 卷26 長孫肥 尉古真
title.raw: 卷26 長孫肥 尉古真 Volume 26: Zhang Sunfei, Weu Guzhen

sentences.zh: 長孫肥 尉古真

translations.literal: Changsun Fei; Wei Guzhen
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Changsun Fei and Wei Guzhen

sentences.zh: 長孫肥，代人也。

translations.literal: Changsun Fei was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Fei came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 昭成時，年十三，以選內侍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhaocheng's reign, at age thirteen he was chosen as inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, in the reign of Emperor Zhaocheng, he was selected to serve within the palace.

sentences.zh: 少有雅度，果毅少言。

translations.literal: In youth he had refined bearing; resolute and sparing of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he carried himself with quiet dignity—decisive, steady, and not given to many words.

sentences.zh: 太祖之在獨孤及賀蘭部，肥常侍從，禦侮左右，太祖深信仗之。

translations.literal: When Taizu was among the Dugu and Helan tribes, Fei constantly attended him, warding off insult at his side; Taizu deeply trusted and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu still lived among the Dugu and the Helan, Fei stayed at his side day and night, shielding him from affront; Taizu came to trust him as one trusts a weapon in the hand.

sentences.zh: 登國初，與莫題等俱為大將，從征劉顯，自濡源擊庫莫奚，討賀蘭部，並有戰功。

translations.literal: At the opening of Dengguo, with Mo Ti and others he was made great general; he followed the campaign against Liu Xian, from Ruyuan struck the Kumo Xi, and subdued the Helan tribe—all with battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dengguo era began he stood among the great generals with Mo Ti and the rest: he marched against Liu Xian, struck the Kumo Xi from Ruyuan, and brought down the Helan—each campaign adding to his name.

sentences.zh: 太祖征蠕蠕，大破之，肥降其主匹候跋，事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: Taizu campaigned against the Rouran and broke them utterly; Fei received the surrender of their lord Pihouba—the affair is set forth in the Rouran annals.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizu's campaign against the Rouran, which shattered them utterly, Fei took the surrender of their lord Pihouba; the full account is in the Rouran biography.

sentences.zh: 又從征衞辰及薛干部，破滅之。

translations.literal: He also followed the campaigns against Wei Chen and the Xuegan tribe and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again against Wei Chen and the Xuegan and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕別主縕紇提子曷多汗等率部落棄父西走，肥以輕騎追至上郡，斬之。

translations.literal: A Rouran splinter lord, Wenheti's son Heduo Han and others, led their clans in abandoning their father and fleeing west; Fei with light cavalry pursued to Shangjun and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenheti's son Heduo Han and other splinter chiefs dragged their clans westward, deserting their father, Fei overtook them at Shangjun with a flying column and took Heduo Han's head.

sentences.zh: 後從征中山，拜中領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against Zhongshan and was appointed Central Army Commander-General.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the siege of Zhongshan and was named Central Army Commander-General.

sentences.zh: 車駕次晉陽，慕容寶并州刺史、遼西王農棄城宵遁，肥追之至蒲泉，獲其妻子。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Jinyang; Murong Bao's inspector of Bingzhou and Prince of Liaoxi Nong abandoned the city and fled by night; Fei pursued to Puquan and seized his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When the court paused at Jinyang, Murong Bao's Bingzhou inspector and Prince of Liaoxi, Nong, slipped from the walls under cover of dark; Fei ran him down to Puquan and took wife and children.

sentences.zh: 太祖將圍中山，慕容寶棄城奔和龍。

translations.literal: Taizu was about to invest Zhongshan; Murong Bao abandoned the city and fled to Helong.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu closed in on Zhongshan, Murong Bao fled the city for Helong.

sentences.zh: 肥與左將軍李栗三千騎追之，至范陽，不及而還。

translations.literal: Fei with the Left General Li Li and three thousand horse pursued to Fanyang, did not overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fei and the Left General Li Li rode three thousand after him as far as Fanyang; they could not catch him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 遂破其研城戍，俘千餘人。

translations.literal: He then broke the Yancheng garrison and took more than a thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He then stormed the Yancheng garrison and carried off more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 中山城內人立慕容普隣為主，太祖圍之。

translations.literal: Within Zhongshan the people set up Murong Pulin as lord; Taizu invested the city.
translations.idiomatic: The folk inside Zhongshan raised Murong Pulin as their leader while Taizu tightened the ring about the walls.

sentences.zh: 普隣乃出步卒千餘人，欲伺間犯圍。

translations.literal: Pulin then sent out more than a thousand foot soldiers, intending to watch for an opening and strike the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Pulin sent out a thousand foot soldiers, hoping to catch the siege at a weak moment and break through.

sentences.zh: 太祖命肥挑戰，偽退，普隣眾追肥，太祖截其後，盡擒斬之。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Fei to offer challenge and feign retreat; Pulin's host pursued Fei, and Taizu cut their rear—all were seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had Fei offer battle and then feign flight; when Pulin's men rushed after Fei, Taizu closed on their rear and took every man—none left alive.

sentences.zh: 時以士馬少糧，遂罷中山之圍，就穀河間。

translations.literal: At the time, with few troops and horses and short of grain, they lifted the siege of Zhongshan and drew provisions from Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies and horses were thin; the siege of Zhongshan was raised, and the army fed itself from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 慕容賀隣殺普隣而自立。

translations.literal: Murong Helin killed Pulin and set himself up as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Helin slew Pulin and declared himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 車駕次魯口，遣肥帥七千騎襲中山，入其郛而還。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Lukou and sent Fei at the head of seven thousand horse to strike Zhongshan; he entered the outer wards and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court camped at Lukou and sent Fei with seven thousand riders to raid Zhongshan; he broke into the outer city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賀隣以步騎四千追肥至泒水，肥自魏昌擊之，獲鎧騎二百。

translations.literal: Helin with four thousand foot and horse pursued Fei to the Bosi River; Fei from Weichang struck them and took two hundred armored riders.
translations.idiomatic: Helin came after him with four thousand foot and horse as far as the Bosi River; Fei wheeled from Weichang, struck, and seized two hundred armored riders.

sentences.zh: 肥中流矢，瘡重，乃還。

translations.literal: Fei was struck by a stray arrow; the wound was grave, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: A shaft found Fei; the wound was deep, and he had to turn back.

sentences.zh: 中山平，以功賜爵琅邪公。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified, for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell, his service won him the ducal title of Langye.

sentences.zh: 遷衞尉卿，改爵盧鄉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Guard and his enfeoffment changed to Luxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Commandant of the Guard, and his fief was changed to Luxiang.

sentences.zh: 時中山太守仇儒不樂內徙，亡匿趙郡，推羣盜趙准為主。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhongshan prefect Qiu Ru was unwilling to move inward; he hid himself in Zhao commandery and set up the bandit chief Zhao Zhun as leader.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongshan prefect Qiu Ru, loath to be resettled inland, vanished into Zhao commandery and made the outlaw Zhao Zhun his figurehead.

sentences.zh: 妄造妖言云：「燕東傾，趙當續，欲知其名，淮水不足。

translations.literal: He falsely forged demonic words, saying: "Yan tilts eastward; Zhao shall continue. To know the name—Huai waters are not enough."
translations.idiomatic: He invented a sorcerer's prophecy: "The Yan realm leans east; Zhao will rise in its place. Would you know the name? The Huai cannot hold it all."

sentences.zh: 」准喜而從之，自號使持節、征西大將軍、青冀二州牧、鉅鹿公，儒為長史，聚黨二千餘人，據關城，連引丁零，殺害長吏，扇動常山、鉅鹿、廣平諸郡。

translations.literal: Zhun rejoiced and followed him; he styled himself Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, Duke of Julu—Ru as chief clerk; they gathered a party of more than two thousand, held Guancheng, linked with the Dingling, killed chief officials, and stirred Changshan, Julu, and Guangping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun took the bait and followed; he called himself Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qing and Ji, Duke of Julu, with Ru as chief clerk. More than two thousand men rallied at Guancheng, the Dingling were drawn in, magistrates were cut down, and rebellion spread through Changshan, Julu, and Guangping.

sentences.zh: 遣肥率三千騎討之，破准於九門，斬仇儒，生擒准。

translations.literal: Fei was sent at the head of three thousand horse to suppress them; he broke Zhun at Jiumen, beheaded Qiu Ru, and took Zhun alive.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was dispatched with three thousand horse, shattered Zhun at Jiumen, struck off Qiu Ru's head, and brought Zhun in bonds.

sentences.zh: 詔以儒肉食，准傳送京師，轘之於市，夷其族。

translations.literal: An edict made Ru's flesh food; Zhun was sent to the capital, drawn and quartered in the market, and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Ru's flesh was made a public feast; Zhun was sent to the capital, torn apart in the market, and his house rooted out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 除肥鎮遠將軍、兗州刺史，給步騎二萬，南徇許昌，略地至彭城。

translations.literal: Fei was appointed Pacification of Distant Regions General and inspector of Yanzhou, given twenty thousand foot and horse; he marched south on Xuchang and carried the frontier to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was named Pacification of Distant Regions General and inspector of Yanzhou, given twenty thousand foot and horse; he drove south against Xuchang and pushed the border to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 司馬德宗將劉該遣使詣肥請降，貢其方物。

translations.literal: Sima Dezong's general Liu Gai sent envoys to Fei to surrender and presented the products of his region.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gai, a Jin general under Sima Dezong, sent envoys to offer surrender to Fei and sent tribute from his district.

sentences.zh: 姚平之寇平陽，太祖將討之，選諸將無加肥者，乃徵還京師，遣肥與毗陵王順等六萬騎為前鋒。

translations.literal: Yao Ping raided Pingyang; Taizu was about to campaign against him and, choosing among the generals, found none to surpass Fei; he summoned Fei back to the capital and sent Fei with the Prince of Piling Shun and others—sixty thousand horse—as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Ping struck at Pingyang, Taizu prepared to march against him; among all his captains none outranked Fei, so Fei was recalled to the capital and sent ahead with Prince of Piling Shun and the rest—sixty thousand horse in the van.

sentences.zh: 車駕次永安，平募遣勇將，率精騎二百闚軍，肥逆擊擒之，匹馬不返。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Yong'an; Ping recruited brave officers who led two hundred picked horse to spy on the army; Fei met them in counterattack and seized them—not a single horse returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court paused at Yong'an; Ping sent daring officers with two hundred elite riders to probe the host; Fei met them head-on and took every man—not one horse rode back.

sentences.zh: 平退保柴壁，太祖進攻屠之。

translations.literal: Ping withdrew to hold Chaibi; Taizu advanced, attacked, and slaughtered the place.
translations.idiomatic: Ping fell back to Chaibi; Taizu pressed the siege and took the city by storm.

sentences.zh: 遣肥還鎮兗州。

translations.literal: Fei was sent back to garrison Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was returned to his post at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 肥撫慰河南，得吏民心，威信著於淮泗。

translations.literal: Fei comforted the people south of the Yellow River, winning the hearts of officials and commoners; his authority and trust stood out along the Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river he soothed the land and won officials and people alike; along the Huai and the Si his name was law.

sentences.zh: 善策謀，勇冠諸將，每戰常為士卒先，前後征討，未嘗失敗，故每有大難，令肥當之。

translations.literal: Skilled in stratagem, foremost in courage among the generals, in every battle he commonly went before the soldiers as their vanguard; in campaigns before and after he never knew defeat—hence whenever great peril arose, they set Fei to face it.
translations.idiomatic: Clever in counsel and first in valor among the captains, he habitually led from the front; campaign after campaign he never tasted defeat—so whenever disaster loomed, it was Fei they sent to meet it.

sentences.zh: 南平中原，西摧羌寇，肥功居多，賞賜奴婢數百口，畜物以千計。

translations.literal: In pacifying the central plains southward and crushing Qiang raiders westward, Fei's merit was greatest; he was rewarded with several hundred household slaves and livestock counted by the thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Of the work that subdued the central plains and broke the Qiang in the west, Fei's share was the largest; reward came in hundreds of bondsmen and herds numbered in thousands.

sentences.zh: 後降爵為藍田侯。

translations.literal: Later his noble rank was reduced to Marquis of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was lowered to Marquis of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 天賜五年卒，諡曰武，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianci he died; posthumous name Wu; buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Tianci, was given the posthumous name Wu, and was laid to rest with honor beside Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子翰襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Han inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han succeeded to the fief.

sentences.zh: 翰，少有父風。

translations.literal: Han in youth had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Han bore his father's stamp.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，以善騎射，為獵郎。

translations.literal: In Taizu's time, for skill in mounted archery he was made hunting attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu his riding and bow won him a place as hunting attendant.

sentences.zh: 太宗之在外，翰與元磨渾等潛謀奉迎。

translations.literal: When Taizong was still abroad, Han with Yuan Mohun and others secretly plotted to welcome and install him.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong was still in exile, Han joined Yuan Mohun and others in a secret plan to bring him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，遷散騎常侍，與磨渾等拾遺左右。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Han was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary; with Mohun and others he attended to remonstrance at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession Han became attendant-in-ordinary; he and Mohun and the rest kept watch at the emperor's ear.

sentences.zh: 以功遷平南將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Pacify-the-South General.
translations.idiomatic: Merit raised him to Pacify-the-South General.

sentences.zh: 率眾鎮北境，威名甚著，蠕蠕憚之。

translations.literal: He led forces to garrison the northern frontier; his renown was very great, and the Rouran feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He took command on the northern marches; his name alone made the Rouran uneasy.

sentences.zh: 後為都督北部諸軍事、平北將軍、真定侯，給殿中細拾隊，加旌旗鼓吹。

translations.literal: Later he was made overseer of all military affairs in the north, Pacify-the-North General, and Marquis of Zhending; he was given the palace's fine picket company and the honor of banners, drums, and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: He was later named overseer of northern armies, Pacify-the-North General, and Marquis of Zhending, with the palace's elite picket and the full panoply of banners, drums, and pipes.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕每犯塞，翰拒擊有功，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Whenever the Rouran raided the frontier, Han repelled them with merit and was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Each Rouran raid on the border met Han's counterstroke and added to his honors until he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，徵還京師，進封平陽王，加安集將軍。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Han was summoned back to the capital, advanced to Prince of Pingyang, and given the additional title Pacification General.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession Han was recalled to the capital, made Prince of Pingyang, and given the added title Pacification General.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕大檀之入寇雲中，世祖親征之，遣翰率北部諸將尉眷，自參合以北，擊大檀別帥阿伏干於柞山，斬首數千級，獲馬萬餘匹。

translations.literal: When the Rouran Datán raided Yunzhong, Shizu campaigned in person and sent Han at the head of the northern generals Wei Juan; from north of Canhe they struck Datán's splinter chief Afugan at Zuo Mountain, beheading several thousand and taking more than ten thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Datán of the Rouran struck Yunzhong, Shizu marched in person and sent Han with the northern commanders, including Wei Juan; north of Canhe they fell on Datán's lieutenant Afugan at Zuo Mountain, taking thousands of heads and more than ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 又與東平公娥青出長川以討大檀。

translations.literal: He also with the Eastern Peace Duke E Qing went out along the Chang River to campaign against Datán.
translations.idiomatic: He also marched along the Chang River with the Eastern Peace Duke, E Qing, to hunt Datán.

sentences.zh: 大檀眾北遁，追擊，克獲而還。

translations.literal: Datán's host fled north; they pursued, seized the booty, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Datán's army ran north; the pursuers gathered the spoils and came home.

sentences.zh: 尋遷司徒。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 襲赫連昌，破之。

translations.literal: He attacked Helian Chang and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Helian Chang and shattered him.

sentences.zh: 世祖復征昌，翰與廷尉道生、宗正娥清率騎三萬為前驅。

translations.literal: Shizu again campaigned against Chang; Han with the Director of Justice Daosheng and the Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing led thirty thousand horse as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu marched on Chang again, Han with Daosheng the Director of Justice and E Qing the Director of the Imperial Clan rode thirty thousand ahead of the host.

sentences.zh: 昌戰敗，奔上邽，翰以八千騎追之，至高平，不及而還。

translations.literal: Chang was defeated and fled to Shanggui; Han with eight thousand horse pursued to Gaoping, did not overtake him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chang broke and ran for Shanggui; Han with eight thousand chased as far as Gaoping, failed to catch him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 從襲蠕蠕，車駕度漠，大檀奔走。

translations.literal: He followed the strike against the Rouran; the imperial carriage crossed the desert, and Datán fled.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Rouran; the court crossed the desert and Datán fled before them.

sentences.zh: 其弟匹黎率眾赴之，遇翰交戰，匹黎眾潰走，斬其渠帥數百人。

translations.literal: His younger brother Pili led forces to join him; meeting Han in battle, Pili's host collapsed and fled; several hundred of their chieftains were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Datán's brother Pili came up with an army; Han met him in battle, broke the host, and struck off the heads of several hundred chieftains.

sentences.zh: 翰清正嚴明，善撫將士，太祖甚重之。

translations.literal: Han was upright, pure, and sternly clear; skilled in comforting generals and soldiers; Taizu greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, incorruptible, and severe in judgment, yet gentle with his officers and men, Han stood high in Taizu's esteem.

sentences.zh: 神䴥三年薨，深見悼惜，為之流涕，親臨其喪，禮依安城王叔孫俊故事，賻賜有加。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenju he died; the court mourned him deeply, wept for him, attended his funeral in person, and the rites followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun, with added funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Shenju; the throne grieved openly, wept at his bier, came in person to the mourning hall, and ordered rites after the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun, with gifts beyond the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Wei; buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Wei and buried with honor beside Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子平成，襲爵，降為公。

translations.literal: His son Pingcheng inherited the enfeoffment and was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pingcheng succeeded to the fief, which was lowered to a ducal house.

sentences.zh: 平成，少以父任為中散，累遷南部尚書。

translations.literal: Pingcheng in youth, through his father's position, was made palace attendant; he rose in succession to southern minister.
translations.idiomatic: Young Pingcheng entered service through his father's rank as palace attendant and climbed to southern minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was laid to rest with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子渾，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Hun inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hun took up the fief.

sentences.zh: 渾，初為中散，久之為彭城鎮將。

translations.literal: Hun at first was palace attendant; after a long while he became garrison commandant of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hun began as palace attendant; in time he was made garrison commandant of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太和中卒。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Taihe reign.

sentences.zh: 子盛襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Sheng inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 翰弟受興。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Shouxing.
translations.idiomatic: Han had a younger brother, Shouxing.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，從征平涼，以功賜爵長進子，除河間太守。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time he followed the campaign against Pingliang; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Changjin and appointed governor of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu he marched on Pingliang; merit made him Marquis of Changjin and governor of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He perished.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子安都，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Andu inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Andu succeeded to the fief.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，為典馬令。

translations.literal: In Xianzu's time he was director of the imperial stud.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzu he directed the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 子頭，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tou inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，為中散，遷內行長，典龍牧曹。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time he was palace attendant, then transferred to director of the inner palace and overseer of the dragon-herd office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he served as palace attendant, then as director of the inner palace and overseer of the dragon-herd herds.

sentences.zh: 天安初卒。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tian'an he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Tian'an era.

sentences.zh: 子拔襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ba inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ba took up the fief.

sentences.zh: 陳弟蘭。

translations.literal: Chen, younger brother of Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was the younger brother of Lan.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，為中散。

translations.literal: At the opening of Shizu's reign he was palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu first took power he entered the palace as attendant.

sentences.zh: 常從征伐，典御兵器，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: He constantly followed campaigns, oversaw imperial weapons, and received very rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He rode on campaign after campaign, kept charge of the imperial armory, and was rewarded again and again.

sentences.zh: 後以破平涼功，賜爵睢陽子，加奮武將軍。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in breaking Pingliang, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Suiyang and given the additional title Inspiring Martial Might General.
translations.idiomatic: Merit at the fall of Pingliang won him Marquis of Suiyang and the added rank Inspiring Martial Might General.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、北部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary and northern minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant-in-ordinary and northern minister.

sentences.zh: 後除豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later named inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He expired.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子烏孤，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Wugu inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wugu inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，出為武都鎮將，入為散令。

translations.literal: At the opening of Gaozu's reign he went out as garrison commandant of Wudu and entered the court as casual attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu began his reign he was posted to Wudu as garrison commandant, then recalled to serve as casual attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 子樂，孝靜時，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Yue, in Xiaojing's time, was Grand Master of Splendorous Golden Light.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue, under Emperor Xiaojing, held the rank Grand Master of Splendorous Golden Light.

sentences.zh: 肥弟亦干，太祖初，為羽林郎。

translations.literal: Fei's younger brother Yigan; at the opening of Taizu's reign he was guardsman of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Fei had a younger brother, Yigan, who at the founding of Taizu's rule served in the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，除廣平太守。

translations.literal: He followed the pacification of the central plains and was appointed governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He marched in the conquest of the central plains and was made governor of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He met his end.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子石洛，世祖初，為羽林郎，稍遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Shiluo; at the opening of Shizu's reign he was guardsman of the Feathered Forest and gradually rose to attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiluo entered the Feathered Forest under Shizu and in time became attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 從征赫連昌，為都將，以功拜樂部尚書，賜爵臨淮公，加寧西將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helian Chang as commander of the van; for merit he was appointed Minister of Music, enfeoffed Duke of Linhuai, and given the additional title Pacify-the-West General.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Helian Chang as a front commander; merit made him Minister of Music, Duke of Linhuai, and Pacify-the-West General.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中卒，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In Shenju he died; posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Shenju era and was posthumously named Jian.

sentences.zh: 子真，少以父任為中散。

translations.literal: His son Zhen in youth, through his father's position, was made palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen, young, entered through his father's rank as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征平涼，以功賜爵臨城子，拜員外散騎侍郎、廣武將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Pingliang; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Lincheng and appointed supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and Broad Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: On the Pingliang campaign merit won him Marquis of Lincheng, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, and Broad Martial General.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵，降為建義將軍、臨淮侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's enfeoffment, reduced to Establish Righteousness General and Marquis of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father's title, lowered to Establish Righteousness General and Marquis of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 遷司衞監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to director of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 征蓋吳。

translations.literal: He campaigned against Gai Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Gai Wu.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat and given the additional title attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Director of the Palace Secretariat with the added rank of attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 從駕征劉義隆，至江。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial campaign against Liu Yilong, reaching the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He rode with the imperial host against Liu Yilong as far as the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 進爵南康公，加冠軍將軍，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Duke of Nankang; he was given the additional rank General Who Champions the State and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Nankang, made general who champions the state, and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 子吳兒，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Wu'er inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu'er inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，為中散、武川鎮將。

translations.literal: At the opening of Gaozu's reign he was palace attendant and garrison commandant of Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu began his reign he served as palace attendant and commandant of the Wuchuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 太和初，卒，贈恒州刺史。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Taihe era he died; posthumously made Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe era he died and was posthumously named inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 子長樂，襲。

translations.literal: His son Changle succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changle succeeded.

sentences.zh: 坐事爵除。

translations.literal: For an offense his enfeoffment was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense his title was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 後歷陵江將軍、羽林監。

translations.literal: Later he held the posts of General of Lingjiang and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as general of Lingjiang and superintendent of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 子榮族，武定中，征西將軍、繁昌男。

translations.literal: His son Rongzu, in the Wuding era, was General Who Campaigns West and Baron of Fanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongzu, in the Wuding era, was general who campaigns west and baron of Fanchang.

sentences.zh: 吳兒弟突，朔州長史。

translations.literal: Wu'er's younger brother Tu was chief clerk of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu'er's younger brother Tu was chief clerk of Shuozhou, the record states.

sentences.zh: 子元慶，平州倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yuanqing was registrar of the granary office in Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanqing was registrar of the granary office in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尉古真，代人也。

translations.literal: Wei Guzhen was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guzhen came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 太祖之在賀蘭部，賀染干遣侯引乙突等詣行宮，將肆逆。

translations.literal: When Taizu was among the Helan tribes, He Rangan sent Houyin Yitu and others to the mobile palace intending treason.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu still lived among the Helan, He Rangan sent Houyin Yitu and others to the traveling palace to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 古真知之，密以馳告，侯引等不敢發。

translations.literal: Guzhen learned of it and secretly reported by swift messenger; Houyin and the rest did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhen learned of the plot and sent word in secret; Houyin and his party never dared move.

sentences.zh: 染干疑古真泄其謀，乃執栲之，以兩車軸押其頭，傷一目，不伏，乃免之。

translations.literal: Rangan suspected Guzhen had leaked the plot, seized him and beat him with the cudgel, pressing two chariot axles against his head and injuring one eye; he would not confess and was therefore released.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan, suspecting Guzhen had betrayed him, had him seized and beaten with the cudgel; two chariot axles were pressed to his head and one eye was ruined, yet he would not confess and was let go.

sentences.zh: 登國初，從征庫莫奚及叱突隣，並有功。

translations.literal: At the opening of Dengguo he followed campaigns against the Kumo Xi and Chitulin, both with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dengguo era opened he marched against the Kumo Xi and Chitulin and won merit in both.

sentences.zh: 又從救賀蘭，破衞辰子直力鞮，復擊慕容寶於參合陂。

translations.literal: He also followed the relief of Helan, defeated Wei Chen's son Zhilidi, and again struck Murong Bao at Canhe Slope.
translations.idiomatic: He also rode to relieve Helan, broke Wei Chen's son Zhilidi, and struck Murong Bao again at Canhe Slope.

sentences.zh: 又從平中原，以功賜爵束州侯，加建節將軍。

translations.literal: He again followed the pacification of the central plains; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongzhou and made commissioner bearing the Staff of Authority.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again in the conquest of the central plains; merit made him Marquis of Dongzhou and commissioner with the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為鴻飛將軍，率眾五千，鎮大洛城。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taizong's reign he was General of Soaring Flight, leading five thousand men to garrison Daluo city.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was General of Soaring Flight, commanding five thousand men at Daluo.

sentences.zh: 太宗西巡，古真與奚斤等率前軍討越勒部，[2]大破之，獲馬五萬匹，牛羊二十萬頭，掠二萬餘家西還。

translations.literal: On Taizong's western tour, Guzhen with Xi Jin and others led the vanguard to chastise the Yuele tribe,[2] routing them utterly; they took fifty thousand horses, two hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep, and drove more than twenty thousand families west in plunder.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizong's western progress Guzhen and Xi Jin led the van against the Yuele tribe[2] and shattered them, taking fifty thousand horses, two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, and herding more than twenty thousand households west as booty.

sentences.zh: 泰常三年，除定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taichang he was made Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang year 3 he was named inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，子億萬襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Yiwani inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Yiwani succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，子盛襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Sheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Sheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 古真弟太真，太宗初，為平南將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Guzhen's younger brother Taizhen, at the opening of Taizong's reign, was General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhen's younger brother Taizhen, when Taizong took power, was general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太真弟諾，少侍太祖，以忠謹著稱。

translations.literal: Taizhen's younger brother Nuo, in youth attending Taizu, was famed for loyalty and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen's younger brother Nuo had attended Taizu from boyhood and was famed for loyal care.

sentences.zh: 從圍中山，諾先登，傷一目。

translations.literal: In the siege of Zhongshan, Nuo was first up the wall and lost an eye.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Zhongshan Nuo was first over the wall and lost an eye.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎曰：「諾兄弟並毀其目，以建功效，誠可嘉也。

translations.literal: Taizu sighed and said: "Nuo and his brothers have each ruined an eye to build achievement—truly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sighed and said, "The Nuo brothers have each cost an eye in service—worthy of praise indeed.

sentences.zh: 」寵待遂隆。

translations.literal: " Favor and attendance then rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " Honor and favor followed in full measure.

sentences.zh: 除平東將軍，賜爵安樂子。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed Viscount of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the east and enfeoffed as viscount of Anle.

sentences.zh: 從討姚平，還，拜國部大人。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Yao Ping, on his return he was appointed Grandee of the National Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against Yao Ping he returned and was named grandee of the national tribes.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為幽州刺史，加東統將軍，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taizong's reign he was Inspector of Youzhou, with the added title General of Eastern Command, and his enfeoffment advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was inspector of Youzhou, given the added rank general of eastern command, and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 長孫道生之討馮跋也，諾與驍騎將軍延普率師次遼西。

translations.literal: In Changsun Daosheng's campaign against Feng Ba, Nuo with the Valiant Cavalry General Yan Pu led troops stationed in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsun Daosheng marched against Feng Ba, Nuo and the Valiant Cavalry General Yan Pu held the line in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 轉寧東將軍，進爵武陵公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and his title advanced to Duke of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to general who pacifies the east and advanced to Duke of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 諾之在州，有惠政，民吏追思之。

translations.literal: While Nuo held the province he had benevolent rule; officials and commoners cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: In his years in the province Nuo governed with kindness; officials and people alike kept his memory.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，薊人張廣達等二百餘人詣闕請之，復除安東將軍、幽州刺史，改邑遼西公。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time more than two hundred men of Ji, including Zhang Guangda, came to court to request him; he was again made General Who Establishes the East and Inspector of Youzhou, with his fief changed to Duke of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu more than two hundred men of Ji, Zhang Guangda among them, came to court to ask for him back; he was again named general who establishes the east and inspector of Youzhou, with his fief changed to Duke of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並為方伯，當世榮之。

translations.literal: The brothers alike became frontier governors—a glory of their day.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers alike held frontier commanderies—a glory of their age.

sentences.zh: 燕土亂久，民戶凋散，諾在州前後十數年，還業者萬餘家。

translations.literal: The Yan region had long been in disorder and households scattered; in his ten-odd years in the province Nuo brought back more than ten thousand families to their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been torn by years of disorder and empty villages; in a decade or more in office Nuo brought more than ten thousand households back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 延和中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Yanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Yanhe era, the record states.

sentences.zh: 第八子觀，[3]襲爵。

translations.literal: His eighth son Guan[3] inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth son Guan[3] inherited the title, the record states.

sentences.zh: 卒，子崘襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Lun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Lun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 又為安北將軍，出鎮北境。

translations.literal: Juan was also made General Who Pacifies the North and went out to garrison the northern marches.
translations.idiomatic: Juan was also named general who pacifies the north and sent to hold the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 與平陽王長孫翰擊蠕蠕別帥阿伏干於祚山，率師至歌刪山，擊蠕蠕別帥便度弟庫仁直，引師而北。

translations.literal: With the Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han he struck the Rouran splinter chief Afugan at Zuo Mountain; he led the army to Geshan mountain and struck the Rouran splinter chief Biandu's younger brother Kurenzhi, then drew the host north.
translations.idiomatic: With the Prince of Pingyang, Changsun Han, he fell on the Rouran lieutenant Afugan at Zuo Mountain, then marched to Geshan and struck Biandu's younger brother Kurenzhi before turning the army north.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕部帥莫孤率高車騎五千乘來逆，眷擊破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: The Rouran tribal chief Mogao led five thousand Gaoche horse to oppose him; Juan routed them and took heads numbering more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran chief Mogao came against him with five thousand Gaoche riders; Juan broke them and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又從征蠕蠕。

translations.literal: He again followed a campaign against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 眷出白、黑兩漠之間，擊其東部，大獲而還。

translations.literal: Juan ranged between the white and black deserts and struck their eastern division, taking a great booty and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Juan ranged between the white and black deserts, struck the eastern Rouran, and came home with heavy spoils.

sentences.zh: 又從征赫連昌，眷出南道，擊昌於上邽。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Helian Chang; Juan took the southern route and struck Chang at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Helian Chang; Juan took the southern road and struck Chang at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 士眾乏糧，臨淮公丘堆等督租於郡縣，為昌所敗。

translations.literal: Soldiers and multitudes lacked grain; the Duke of Linhuai Qiu Dui and others levied grain rents in the commanderies and counties and were defeated by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: The army ran short of grain; the Duke of Linhuai, Qiu Dui, and others gathered rents in the commanderies and were beaten by Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌乘勝抄掠，諸將患之。

translations.literal: Chang pressed his victory in raiding and plunder; the generals were all worried.
translations.idiomatic: Chang pressed his victory in raids and plunder, and the commanders grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 眷與侍御史安頡陰謀設伏，邀擊擒昌。

translations.literal: Juan with Attending Censor An Pi secretly set an ambush, intercepted and captured Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Juan and the attending censor An Pi laid an ambush in secret, intercepted Chang, and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 以功拜寧北將軍，加散騎常侍，進爵漁陽公。

translations.literal: For merit he was made General Who Pacifies the North, added Palace Attendant, and his title advanced to Duke of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Merit made him general who pacifies the north and palace attendant, and his title rose to Duke of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: [4]後從征和龍，眷督萬騎前驅，慰喻降二千餘戶。

translations.literal: [4] Later he followed the campaign against Helong; Juan directed ten thousand riders as vanguard and soothed more than two thousand surrendering households.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Later, on the Helong campaign, Juan led ten thousand horse as vanguard and won over more than two thousand surrendering households.

sentences.zh: 尋為假節，加侍中，都督豫洛二州及河內諸軍事、安南將軍、開府，鎮虎牢。

translations.literal: Soon he held credential staff as acting commissioner, was added Palace Attendant, and as commander supervised military affairs in Yu and Luo and within Henei; he was General Who Pacifies the South, opened a bureau, and garrisoned Hubao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he bore the staff as acting commissioner, was added palace attendant, and as commander oversaw armies in Yu, Luo, and Henei; he was general who pacifies the south, opened a bureau, and held Hubao.

sentences.zh: 張掖王禿髮保周之反也，徵眷與永昌王健等率師討之，破保周於番禾。

translations.literal: When Tufa Baozhou, Prince of Zhangye, rebelled, Juan was summoned with Prince of Yongchang Jian and others to lead troops against him, routing Baozhou at Fanhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Tufa Baozhou, Prince of Zhangye, rebelled, Juan was called up with the Prince of Yongchang, Jian, and others; they broke Baozhou at Fanhe.

sentences.zh: 保周遁走，眷率騎追之，保周窮迫自殺。

translations.literal: Baozhou fled; Juan led cavalry in pursuit until Baozhou, driven to extremity, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhou fled; Juan rode after him until, cornered, Baozhou took his own life.

sentences.zh: 詔眷留鎮涼州，加都督涼沙河三州諸軍事、安西將軍，領護羌戎校尉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Juan to remain and garrison Liangzhou, with added command of military affairs in Liang, Sha, and He provinces as General Who Pacifies the West and as protector of the Qiang and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict left Juan to garrison Liangzhou, with added command of Liang, Sha, and He armies as general who pacifies the west and protector of the Qiang and Rong.

sentences.zh: 轉敦煌鎮將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 又擊破吐谷渾，俘三千餘口。

translations.literal: He again routed the Tuyuhun and took more than three thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the Tuyuhun again and took more than three thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 眷歷鎮四蕃，威名並著。

translations.literal: Juan successively garrisoned the four frontiers; his martial name was famed everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Juan held the four marches in turn; his martial name stood out in every quarter.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，率師北擊伊吾，克其城，大獲而還。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time he led troops north to strike Yiwu, took its city, and returned with a great haul.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he marched north against Yiwu, took the city, and returned laden with spoils.

sentences.zh: 尋拜侍中、太尉，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant and his title advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant and grand commandant, and his title rose to prince.

sentences.zh: 與太宰常英等評尚書事。

translations.literal: With the Grand Preceptor Chang Ying and others he reviewed Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With the grand preceptor Chang Ying and others he reviewed affairs in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 高宗北巡狩，以寒雪方降，議還。

translations.literal: On Gaozong's northern imperial hunt, as cold snow was about to fall, there was discussion of turning back.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozong's northern hunt, as bitter snow threatened, the court talked of turning back.

sentences.zh: 眷諫曰：「今動大眾，以威北敵，去都不遠，而便旋駕，虜必疑我有內難。

translations.literal: Juan remonstrated: "Now having moved a great host to overawe the northern enemy, we are not far from the capital—yet if we wheel the imperial carriage, the barbarians will surely suspect we have internal trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Juan remonstrated: "We have moved a great host to overawe the northern foe and are not far from the capital—yet if we wheel the imperial carriage now, the barbarians will surely think we have trouble within.

sentences.zh: 雖方寒雪，兵人勞苦，以經略大體，宜便前進。

translations.literal: Though snow is now bitter and troops suffer hardship, for the larger strategy of state we ought to press forward.
translations.idiomatic: Snow is bitter and the troops suffer, but for the larger strategy of state we ought to press on.

sentences.zh: 」高宗從之，遂渡漠而還。

translations.literal: " Gaozong followed this and crossed the desert on the return.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozong took his counsel and crossed the desert on the homeward march.

sentences.zh: 以眷元老，賜杖履上殿。

translations.literal: As a senior elder Juan was granted staff and shoes to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior elder Juan was granted staff and shoes to enter the hall.

sentences.zh: 和平四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Heping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Heping year 4.

sentences.zh: 高宗悼惜之，贈大將軍，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Gaozong mourned him and posthumously made him Grand General with posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong mourned him and posthumously named him grand general with the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子多侯，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Duohou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duohou succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 多侯少有武幹，顯祖時，為假節、征西將軍、領護羌戎校尉、敦煌鎮將。

translations.literal: Duohou in youth had martial ability; in Xianzu's time he was acting commissioner, General Who Campaigns West, protector of the Qiang and Rong, and garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou in youth showed martial talent; under Xianzu he was acting commissioner, general who campaigns west, protector of the Qiang and Rong, and garrison commissioner of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，上表求率輕騎五千，西入于闐，兼平諸國，因敵取資，平定為效。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he memorialized asking to lead five thousand light cavalry west into Khotan to subdue the various states in passing, taking supplies from the enemy and achieving pacification.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he asked leave to lead five thousand light horse west into Khotan, subduing the western states as he went and feeding his men from the enemy until the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 弗許。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，蠕蠕部帥旡盧真率三萬騎入塞圍鎮，多侯擊之走，以功進號征西大將軍。

translations.literal: At the opening of Gaozu's reign the Rouran tribal chief Jiluzhen led thirty thousand cavalry into the borders to besiege the garrison; Duohou struck and drove them off; for merit his title was advanced to Grand General Who Campaigns West.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession the Rouran chief Jiluzhen led thirty thousand horse into the borders to besiege the garrison; Duohou struck and drove them off, and merit raised him to grand general who campaigns west.

sentences.zh: 後多侯獵于南山，蠕蠕遣部帥度拔入圍敦煌，斷其還路。

translations.literal: Later Duohou was hunting on the southern mountains when the Rouran sent the tribal chief Duba to surround Dunhuang and cut his line of return.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while Duohou hunted the southern mountains, the Rouran sent the chief Duba to surround Dunhuang and cut off his return.

sentences.zh: 多侯且前且戰，遂衝圍而入。

translations.literal: Duohou fought advancing by turns and burst through the encirclement to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou fought as he advanced and broke through the ring into the city.

sentences.zh: 率眾出戰，大破之，追北數十里，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: He led the multitude out to battle, routed them utterly, pursued north several tens of li, and took heads numbering more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men out, routed them utterly, pursued north for tens of li, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 因上疏求北取伊吾，斷蠕蠕通西域之路。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial asking to take Yiwu in the north and sever the Rouran route to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to seize Yiwu in the north and cut the Rouran road to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 高祖善其計，以東作方興，難之。

translations.literal: Gaozu approved the plan but, with eastern works then rising, found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu approved the plan, but with eastern works then rising, could not carry it out.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，為妻元氏所害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he was killed by his wife, Lady Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 1 his wife, Lady Yuan, killed him.

sentences.zh: 子建，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 歷位給事中。

translations.literal: He held office as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons, the record states.

sentences.zh: 建弟那，襲爵。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Na inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Na inherited the title, the record states.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子範，襲。

translations.literal: His son Fan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 範弟顯業，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Xianye was Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Xianye was regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 與太原公主姦通，生子彥。

translations.literal: He committed adultery with the Princess of Taiyuan and begot the son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He lay with the Princess of Taiyuan and fathered a son, Yan.

sentences.zh: 武定中，衞將軍、南營州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was General of the Guard and Inspector of Nanyingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was general of the guard and inspector of Nanyingzhou.

sentences.zh: 多侯弟子慶賓，善騎射，有將略。

translations.literal: Duohou's younger brother's son Qingbin was skilled in mounted archery and had generalship.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou's nephew Qingbin was skilled in mounted archery and showed commander's gifts.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，釋褐員外散騎侍郎，稍遷左將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time he doffed the hemp and was made Outside-the-Gates Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Casual Staff, then gradually rose to Left General and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he doffed the hemp and became outside-the-gates attendant-in-ordinary on the casual staff, then rose by degrees to left general and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，議欲送蠕蠕主阿那瓌還國，慶賓上表固爭，不從。

translations.literal: In Suzong's time, when there was debate on sending the Rouran ruler Anagui back to his country, Qingbin memorialized in firm opposition; the court did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong, when the court debated sending the Rouran ruler Anagui home, Qingbin memorialized in firm opposition; the throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕遂執行臺元孚，大掠北境。

translations.literal: Later the Rouran indeed seized the touring commissioner Yuan Fu and ravaged the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran then seized the touring commissioner Yuan Fu and ravaged the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書令李崇討之，慶賓別將隸崇，出塞而返。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Writing Li Chong to chastise them; Qingbin as a detached commander served under Chong, went beyond the passes, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict set the Minister of Writing Li Chong to chastise them; Qingbin served under him as detached commander, went beyond the passes, and came back.

sentences.zh: 元法僧之外叛，蕭衍遣其豫章王蕭綜鎮徐州，又詔慶賓為別將隸安豐王延明討之。

translations.literal: At Yuan Faseng's defection to the outside Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Zong to garrison Xuzhou; an edict also made Qingbin a detached commander under Prince of Anfeng Yanming to chastise him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng defected, Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Zong, to hold Xuzhou; an edict also made Qingbin detached commander under the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, to strike him.

sentences.zh: 尋除後將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Rear General and Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was rear general and inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時尒朱榮兵威漸盛，曾經肆州，慶賓畏惡之，據城不出。

translations.literal: At that time Erzhu Rong's military prestige was gradually growing; he once passed through Sizhou, and Qingbin, fearing and loathing him, shut the city and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong's military fame was then rising; passing through Sizhou once, he found Qingbin so fearful and hostile that the city gates stayed shut.

sentences.zh: 榮恨慶賓，舉兵襲之。

translations.literal: Rong hated Qingbin and raised troops to assault him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong hated Qingbin and raised troops to take him.

sentences.zh: 慶賓別駕姚和內應，榮遂害慶賓僚屬，拘慶賓還秀容，呼為假父。

translations.literal: Qingbin's aide Yao He colluded within; Rong then killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin and brought him back to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin's aide Yao He opened the gates from within; Rong killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin, and carried him to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."

sentences.zh: 後以母憂還都，尋起為平東將軍、光祿大夫、都督，鎮汝陰。

translations.literal: Later, on returning to the capital for his mother's mourning, he was soon recalled and made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and commander, garrisoning Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after mourning his mother in the capital, he was soon recalled as general who pacifies the east, grand master of splendid happiness, and commander at Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 還朝，永安二年卒。

translations.literal: He returned to court and died in the second year of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court and died in Yong'an year 2.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、雍州刺史，又追加侍中、司空公。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yongzhou; further added Palace Attendant and Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: They posthumously made him general of chariots and cavalry and inspector of Yongzhou, then added palace attendant and duke of works.

sentences.zh: 慶賓子豹，起家員外郎。

translations.literal: Qingbin's son Bao, from youth entered service as Gentleman of the Suite.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin's son Bao began his career as gentleman of the suite.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，行潁州事，與蕭衍將裴之禮戰歿。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he acted for Ying Province and died in battle with Liang general Pei Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he acted for Ying Province and fell fighting Liang general Pei Zhili.

sentences.zh: 豹弟瑾，武定中，東平太守。

translations.literal: Bao's younger brother Jin, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's brother Jin was administrator of Dongping in the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 子長壽，幼拜散騎常侍，遷殿中右曹尚書，仍加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Changshou, while still young was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, transferred to Director of the Right Bureau in the Palace Secretariat, and again added Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changshou, still a boy, was made regular attendant of scattered cavalry, then director of the right bureau in the palace secretariat, and again regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從征劉義隆，至江。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liu Yilong, reaching the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Liu Yilong as far as the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 賜爵會稽公，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Duke of Kuaiji and added General Who Champions the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed duke of Kuaiji and made general who champions the state.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，除涇州刺史。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time he was made Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he was made inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 和平五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Heping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Heping year 5.

sentences.zh: 子彌真，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Mizhen inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mizhen succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 彌真卒，無子。

translations.literal: Mizhen died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhen died childless.

sentences.zh: 弟狀德，襲爵。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhuangde inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhuangde inherited the title, the record states.

sentences.zh: 地干弟侯頭，襲地干職，為庫部尚書。

translations.literal: Diggan's younger brother Hou Tou inherited Diggan's post and was Minister of the Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Diggan's brother Hou Tou succeeded to Diggan's office and became minister of the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 侯頭弟力斤，亦以忠謹聞。

translations.literal: Hou Tou's younger brother Lijin was also known for loyalty and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tou's brother Lijin was likewise famed for loyal care.

sentences.zh: 歷位御史中尉、并州刺史，有政績。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Censor-in-Chief and Inspector of Bing Province and had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor-in-chief and inspector of Bing Province with a record of good government.

sentences.zh: 加冠軍將軍，賜爵晉陽侯。

translations.literal: He was added General Who Champions the State and granted the title Marquis of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who champions the state and enfeoffed as marquis of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平南將軍。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously named general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 力斤弟焉陳，尚書、安樂侯。

translations.literal: Lijin's younger brother Yanchen was Minister of Writing and Marquis of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Lijin's brother Yanchen was minister of writing and marquis of Anle.

sentences.zh: 古真族玄孫聿，字成興，性耿介。

translations.literal: Guzhen's collateral descendant by the sixth generation, Yu, style name Chenxing, was upright by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhen's sixth-generation collateral descendant Yu, styled Chenxing, was stiffly upright.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，為武衞將軍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was general of the martial guard.

sentences.zh: 是時，領軍元叉秉權，百僚莫不致敬，而聿獨長揖不拜。

translations.literal: At that time the army commander Yuan Cha held power; the hundred officials all paid respect, yet Yu alone made a long bow without kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Yuan Cha held the reins; every official bowed low, yet Yu alone gave a long bow and refused to kneel.

sentences.zh: 尋出為平西將軍、東涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Pacification-West General and Inspector of Eastern Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as pacification-west general and inspector of Eastern Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: [5]涼州緋色，天下之最，叉送白綾二千匹，令聿染，拒而不許。

translations.literal: [5] Liangzhou's scarlet dye was the finest under Heaven; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk and ordered Yu to dye them, but he refused and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: [5] Liangzhou produced the finest scarlet in the realm; Cha sent two thousand bolts of white silk to be dyed, and Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 叉諷御史劾之，驛徵至京。

translations.literal: Cha prompted the censor to impeach him; by post he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had the censors impeach him and summoned him to the capital by courier.

sentences.zh: 覆驗無狀，還復任。

translations.literal: On reexamination the charge did not stand, and he returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: A fresh inquiry found no case, and he resumed his post.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於州，時年五十。

translations.literal: Soon he died in the province, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named general who pacifies the north and inspector of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 子儉。

translations.literal: His son Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jian.

sentences.zh: 武定中，開府祭酒。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Opening Office Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was opening-office libationer.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：長孫肥結髮內侍，雄烈知名，軍鋒所指，罔不奔散，關張萬人之敵，未足多也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zhang Sunfei, with hair tied up, served within the palace; fierce and renowned, wherever the army's edge pointed none failed to scatter and flee — foes of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, a match for ten thousand men, would not be too much to praise.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Zhang Sunfei entered palace service still wearing bound hair; his martial fame blazed abroad, and wherever his armies turned enemies broke and ran — even rivals of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei would scarcely outshine him.

sentences.zh: 翰有父風，不隕先構，臨喪加禮，抑有由哉！

translations.literal: Han had his father's bearing, did not let the ancestral structure fall, and at a parent's funeral added ceremony — there was reason for it indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Han bore his father's spirit and did not let the family name decline; the extra rites he observed at mourning had their ground.

sentences.zh: 尉真兄弟，忠勇奮發，義以忘生。

translations.literal: The Wei Guzhen brothers, loyal and brave, stirred themselves to zeal and, for righteousness, forgot life.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei brothers were loyal and fierce, roused to the utmost pitch, and for duty's sake forgot their lives.

sentences.zh: 眷威略著時，增隆家業，青紫麾旄，亦其宜矣！

translations.literal: Juan's martial prestige stood out in his age, augmenting and elevating the clan enterprise — rank robes and command banners were also what was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Juan's renown in arms shone in his day and raised the house higher still — purple rank and commanders' pennons suited such a man.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 追斬至長城下 冊府卷三八一

translations.literal: Pursued and beheaded reaching below the Great Wall. Cefu juan 381
translations.idiomatic: "Pursued and beheaded to below the Great Wall": Cefu, juan 381

sentences.zh: 〈四五二八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4528〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 4528

sentences.zh: 「長城」作「其城」。

translations.literal: "Great Wall" is written as "their city."
translations.idiomatic: "Great Wall" appears as "their city."

sentences.zh: 按和龍距古長城甚遠，疑作「其」是。

translations.literal: Commentary: On examination Helong is very far from the ancient Great Wall; suspecting "their" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Helong lies far from the old Great Wall; "their [city]" is likely right.

sentences.zh: 越勒部 按「勒」當是「勤」之訛，詳卷一一三校記越勒氏條。

translations.literal: Yuele tribe. Commentary: "le" should be the error for "qin"; see the collation entry on the Yuele clan in juan 113.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele tribe: "le" is likely a corruption of "qin"; see the Yuele clan note in juan 113.

sentences.zh: 下同，不再列舉。

translations.literal: The same below; not listed again.
translations.idiomatic: The same below; not listed again, the record states.

sentences.zh: 第八子觀 北史卷二０尉古真傳「觀」作「歡」。

translations.literal: The eighth son Guan. Northern History juan 20, Wei Guzhen biography, reads "Guan" as "Huan."
translations.idiomatic: "The eighth son Guan": Northern History juan 20, Wei Guzhen's life, has "Guan" as "Huan."

sentences.zh: 魏書當因避高歡諱改。

translations.literal: Wei shu must have changed it to avoid the taboo on Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei shu likely altered the name to avoid the taboo on Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 進爵漁陽公 諸本「漁」作「源」。

translations.literal: Advanced to Duke of Yuyang. In various editions "yu" (fish) is written as "yuan" (source).
translations.idiomatic: "Advanced to duke of Yuyang": editions read yu (fish) as yuan (source).

sentences.zh: 北史卷二０作「漁陽王」，節去由公進王事。

translations.literal: Northern History juan 20 reads "Prince of Yuyang" and omits the matter of advancement from duke to prince.
translations.idiomatic: Northern History juan 20 has "prince of Yuyang" and drops the promotion from duke to prince.

sentences.zh: 按卷五高宗紀太安三年正月見「漁陽公尉眷」，和平四年五月書「漁陽王尉眷薨」。

translations.literal: On examination, in juan 5 of the Annals of Emperor Gaozong, in the first month of the third year of Taian appears "Duke of Yuyang Wei Juan," and in the fifth month of the fourth year of Heping it records "Prince of Yuyang Wei Juan died."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong's annals, juan 5, Taian year 3, month 1, records "Duke of Yuyang Wei Juan"; Heping year 4, month 5, records "Prince of Yuyang Wei Juan died."

sentences.zh: 「源陽」無此郡名，今據改。

translations.literal: There is no commandery named Yuanyang; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: No commandery called Yuanyang exists; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 東涼州刺史 北史卷二０無「東」字。

translations.literal: Inspector of Eastern Liangzhou. Northern History juan 20 lacks the character "eastern."
translations.idiomatic: "Inspector of Eastern Liangzhou": Northern History juan 20 omits "eastern."

sentences.zh: 按「東涼州」無考，「東」字當是衍文。

translations.literal: Commentary: "Eastern Liangzhou" is unattested; the character "eastern" must be a superfluous addition.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Eastern Liangzhou" is unattested; "eastern" is likely a stray character.
